claims.class: Inspected implementation and retained observed execution
claims.claim: Refresh expiry can trigger frontend logout while extended access remains valid.
limits: Original refresh remains unreplaced. Each activity cycle needs five quiet seconds.
This does not establish server rejection of still-valid access or a separate backend deadline.

claims.class: Inspected implementation and retained controlled execution
claims.claim: A late ended-session response can persist stale refresh credentials; the candidate skips replacement and rejected recovery clears the fresh session.
limits: Stale refresh needs strictly more than three hours remaining at replacement time.
Revocation and rejection are modeled. The response includes TOKEN_INVALID_EXPIRED, not an arbitrary HTTP 401.
Both versions accept a late response. Candidate replacement behavior worsens the race.
Acquisition and recovery are directly invoked service operations; Home delivery is outside this controlled case.

limits: Deliver the usable response after Timeout mounts but before the one-second logout completes.
The common scheduled-acquisition pair fails in both revisions.
